842: mchammer documents fixed-composition, semi-grand canonical, VCSGC and thermodynamic-integration ensembles. In the semi-grand canonical ensemble the composition is tracked while the chemical-potential difference is varied, and phase boundaries can be located from discontinuous changes. To obtain the free energy across a two-phase region, an appropriate sampling scheme such as VCSGC is chosen. Temperature integration and thermodynamic integration for obtaining free energies are also provided. MC ensembles, free-energy analysis
843: Phases on different parent lattices usually each need their own configurational model. In this workflow, which compares the free energies of all phases on a common reference, the competition with other lattices and with the liquid phase is reconciled separately even when phase boundaries are located by MC alone.
845: As a first approximation, line phases start from the ordered structure + QHA, disordered solid solutions from SQS or similar + QHA + the ideal configurational term, and ordered phases whose composition width is to be examined from the energies of anti-site and vacancy defects. If configurational correlations matter, we move on to icet CE + MC or to swap MC based on a validated interatomic potential. The liquid phase is evaluated with calphy or an existing database, and finally the solubility ranges are determined from the competition among all phases. This is a design decision for this project based on official features and executed examples.

885: Difference between sublattices and a disordered solid solution
886: A sublattice is a way of partitioning crystal sites; a disordered solid solution is a state of elemental occupation. Sublattices are a division of the sites of a single crystal phase according to their role; they are not separate phases. In an ordered solid solution the elements preferentially occupy particular sublattices, and in the completely disordered state such preferential occupation disappears.

912: Sublattices serve to group sites in order to describe the occupation state. For the same parent lattice, the partition changes with the assumed ordering pattern. 913: "Mixed occupation" does not mean placing fractional atoms on one site. In a single configuration each site is occupied by one element, and the occupation fractions of several elements are expressed as a statistical average over a site group or over configurations. Formally each site can also be defined as its own sublattice, but average site fractions alone cannot fully represent the configurational correlations between sites.
